Nothing departed from the plan, so there's no Changed:. The code is one commit rather than several, because revisits and entry anchors share the same restructuring of site.ts.

Chose: Every entry exists before any anchor resolves

where src/site.ts file page

quote // Every entry exists before any anchor resolves, since an anchor can name

Because (Claude, not asked): entries used to be built and resolved in one pass, plan by plan. Tallow anchors pumice, which comes earlier, but tallow's as-built anchors vellum's, which comes later, so one pass can't see it. Two passes: make every entry, then resolve the anchors.

Chose: An entry anchor's link is the target property, apart from place

where src/render.ts file page

quote ? `<p class="target"><span class="label">entry</span> <a rel="anchored-at" itemprop="target" href="${rel(here, ra.entry.doc.href)}#${ra.entry.entry.slug}">${kindTitle(ra.entry.entry)}</a> <span class="meta">in ${docName(ra.entry)}</span></p>`

Because (Claude, not asked): the rel is shared, as the plan says, but the microdata property says what's at the far end. place is a symbol or file page and target is another plan's entry, or a whole plan. An agent can follow anchored-at without caring, or ask for one kind.

Chose: The quoted entry is found by its heading, and shown whole

where src/resolve.ts file page

quote const heading = lines.findIndex((l) => /^## /.test(l) && l.replace(/^## (?:\w+: )?/, '') === title);

Because (Claude, not asked): the plan said the search stays inside the entry. The entry runs from its ## Kind: title line to the next ##, with trailing blank lines dropped. It's shown whole, not as 3 lines of context, because an entry is short and its heading tells the reader which entry this is. For grommet's quote of lanyard, that's lines 34 to 40, with line 39 highlighted.

Chose: A whole-plan anchor makes no back-link on the plan it names

Because (Claude, not asked): the plan gave entries an "Anchored by" line and said nothing about whole plans. The only such anchor is bodkin's, which is cross-repo from aide, so nothing here would exercise a back-link. It waits for an anchor that needs it.

Chose: Code-span unwrapping stays lenient, pinned by a test

where test/plan.test.ts file page

quote // Lenient on purpose: awl (aide 248a2a5) wraps a title that contains

Because (Claude, not asked, at conversion): this was a write-ahead finding in the cart, and conversion has to promote it or drop it. Awl is frozen, and its anchor at grommet only means what its writer meant if the unwrapping is lenient. Strict CommonMark would be more correct and would break a real anchor. How to write a title that contains backticks is a format question, and it belongs to aide.

Answered: Exact entry titles are a stable enough key for anchors between plans

Answer (measured): held, on ten of ten: three in mock-control at f02528f, seven in aide at 248a2a5. One of the ten matched only because phoropter's code-span unwrapping is lenient. Awl's anchor at grommet wraps a title containing backticks in single backticks, which CommonMark would split at the first inner backtick. That's the "backticks written differently" case in this guess, caught by the reader rather than the writer. If the unwrapping is ever made strict, that anchor stops matching.
